mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months, it signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production and housing starts indicates broad economic weakness that reduces corporate revenue expectations, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through joint series interaction.
failure_condition: The joint decline of INDPRO and HOUST does not predict negative returns (Rank IC < 0.02) over any 3-year rolling window, or correlation with returns is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a housing market correction characterized by declining housing starts and rising federal funds rates, consumer confidence falls and retail sales weaken, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST declines and FEDFUNDS rises, or Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases, or Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that triggers monetary policy tightening, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and unemployment rate indicates a monetary tightening cycle coinciding with economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through joint series interaction.
failure_condition: The joint rise of FEDFUNDS and UNRATE does not predict negative returns (Rank IC < 0.02) over any 3-year rolling window, or correlation with returns is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a manufacturing slowdown marked by declining industrial production and rising unemployment, corporate output constraints reduce profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days through joint series interaction.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO declines and UNRATE rises, or Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.
